newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Soccer-Venables picks first Australia squad.
newsitem.headline: Soccer-Venables picks first Australia squad.

text.p: Australia coach Terry Venables on Friday announced a squad including three new players for a four-team tournament in January which will mark the former England soccer manager's first outing in charge of the Socceroos.
Venables will make his first visit to his new coaching homeland on January 3, when he officially takes over from outgoing Australia coach Eddie Thomson.
The squad for the January 18-26 series against New Zealand, Norway and South Korea is made up entirely of players based in Australia.
The new players added to the 22-man squad are Australian national soccer league leading striker David Zdrilic, his Sydney United teammate Mark Babic and Marconi striker Sean Babic.
"Norway, South Korea and New Zealand collectively give us high quality competition and different playing styles," Venables said in a news release.
"It is an ideal opportunity for our players to demonstrate their ability against different and good opposition."
Two matches have been arranged for European-based Australian players, against Croatia in Split in February and against Hungary in Budapest in March.
Thomson resigned last month to take up a lucrative coaching position in Japan's J-League.

Venables says a major motive for accepting the job was to take the team to the 1998 World Cup finals, an opportunity the former Crystal Palace, QPR, Barcelona and Tottenham manager missed when he was in charge of England.

Under a unique coaching arrangement, assistant coach Raul Blanco will oversee players in Australia's national soccer league and report back to Venables, who will spend about four months a year in Australia during his 19-month contract.
